lines: You can ask an AI to be careful with your data. Or you can just not let it choose whose data it touches.
Think of a withdrawal slip. You can write any account number you like. The bank still pays out of the card you swiped.

An AI that saves a note for you sends the app a request: what to save, and where it goes. Let it fill in the where, and one wrong guess, or one sneaky request, puts your note in someone else's account.

Asking it to be careful won't stop that. The app can. It ignores the account the AI wrote and uses whoever is signed in. Send it a request naming someone else's account, and the write still lands in yours. Theirs isn't touched.
One real memory tool takes six fields from the AI. Which conversation the memory belongs to isn't one of them. The server looks that up itself.
Let the AI decide what. Let the app decide whose.
facts: Script v2 (Robin, 2026-10-30, after draft 1: 'no clue what this one is even talking about'; he chose a plain rewrite). II is an analogy, not a claim. III: where-logic-lives, rules that must hold 'if the caller is hostile' and a server that 'does not stop a buggy or hostile client from sending inconsistent identifiers' unless the identifier is derived; mcp-tool-design, a model 'has decent reason to think' chat_id belongs in write_memory (the wrong guess). IV: where-logic-lives, 'enforce it in service code or policy at the data-owning boundary'; workspace from the signed-in context, from the systems repo's storage-routing test (S12): a payload naming workspace B 'lands its write in workspace A (the context's) and leaves B unchanged'. V: mcp-tool-design, write_memory 'declares six properties and requires all six. chat_id is not among them', and its description 'chat_id is NOT an input, it is derived server-side from source_turn_id'. VI: where-logic-lives, 'Let the model choose among safe actions. Reject unsafe states at a boundary the model cannot waive.' Not claimed: that the chat_id derivation gives per-user authorization or tenant isolation (the article says it does not); the account/workspace claim rests on the S12 test only. Draft 1's script and take are kept in vo/audition/.
